findings.title: CTR_DRBG secret state is processed by an explicitly unmasked AES datapath
findings.location: module csrng_block_encrypt, u_aes_cipher_core parameterization and entropy connections
findings.description: The block-encryption engine directly loads the secret 256-bit CTR_DRBG key through key_init[0] and instantiates aes_cipher_core with SecMasking fixed to 1'b0 and NumShares therefore equal to one. Its masking entropy acknowledgement is tied low and entropy data is tied to zero. The default SBoxImpl for csrng_block_encrypt and csrng_core is also the unmasked lookup-table implementation. Consequently, each instantiate, reseed, update, and generate operation performs AES-256 using the DRBG key in an unmasked datapath. A local attacker capable of power or electromagnetic observation can target repeated AES operations to recover the internal DRBG key. Recovery of key and V compromises prediction resistance and can reveal future random values used for cryptographic keys, masks, and nonces. Selecting SBoxImplDom at a higher level would not fix the sharing invariant because SecMasking remains disabled and no fresh entropy is supplied. The source comment that SCA leakage is not considered does not provide a synthesized mitigation.
findings.recommendation: Use a side-channel-hardened block-encryption implementation for CTR_DRBG. Enable end-to-end state and key sharing, provide fresh entropy from EDN, and select the DOM S-Box with its required synthesis-preservation constraints. Do not rely solely on substituting the DOM S-Box while SecMasking is zero. If physical side-channel attacks are intentionally excluded, document and enforce that assumption in the CSRNG threat model and production security configuration, and add a build-time assertion preventing accidental claims that CSRNG internal state is SCA protected.
